result.note: A weekly roundup with thin detail. The questions test the trade measures (steel anti-dumping probe, EU scrap carve-out, bond inflows) and the first defence co-development pact with Japan.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade and capital measures in the week ending 4 July 2026:
items: India opened an anti-dumping probe into steel imports from China, Japan and Russia.
India pressed the European Union for a carve-out on scrap exports.
India drew a record USD 3 billion of foreign bond inflows after scrapping key taxes.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. The steel probe opened on Monday 29 June, the scrap-export request went to Brussels on Tuesday, and the record USD 3 billion of bond money came in by Wednesday after key taxes were scrapped. TBB reads the week as India using rules as a lever to set its own terms of engagement.
questions.source: New Delhi opened an anti-dumping probe into steel from China, Japan, and Russia on Monday, pressed Brussels for a scrap-export carve-out on Tuesday, drew a record USD 3 billion of foreign bond money after scrapping key taxes by Wednesday

questions.prompt: In the week ending 4 July 2026, India signed its first defence co-development pact with which country?
questions.explain: India closed the week by signing a first defence co-development pact with Japan. In the same week, Modi also deepened India's presence in Seychelles with a soft-power package.
questions.source: closed the week signing a first defence co-development pact with Japan
